_description.summary: Pattern-level meta-operations: halting a hex (Charon's, Thanatos), Contemplation, comment handling, Timekeeper, Everbook entries, queue and cassette control, serializing and deserializing patterns, comparing pattern shapes, draw_pattern, raycast variants, special gambits (Ra, Apep, Pollux, Castor), debris and sediment particles.
use_cases: Working with patterns as data (serialize, compare, draw)
Managing the Everbook or queued cassettes

runtime_escape.d: To use Contemplation, I draw it, then another arbitrary pattern. That second pattern is added to the stack.

halt.d: This pattern forcibly halts a Hex. This is mostly useless on its own, as I could simply just stop writing patterns, or put down my staff.

thanatos.d: It seems there is a limit to how many patterns can be evaluated within a single Hex. I can use this pattern to deterime how many patterns remain before I reach this limit.

create_linebreak.d: Adds a line-break comment iota with space-indents of given number to the stack.

switch_comment.d: Transforms input Comment Iota into String Iota, or everything else into Comment Iota; has no effect if **MoreIotas** not installed.

current_tick.d: Adds a number to the stack which seems to be related to how Nature represents time; If I cast the pattern, then cast the same pattern a second later, the number it adds has increased by 20.

everbook/delete.d: Takes a pattern and removes the entry with that pattern key from your Everbook.

everbook/toggle_macro.d: Takes a pattern and marks that entry of your Everbook as a Pattern that when drawn by your hand will be treated as any other of Nature's patterns.

dequeue.d: I can also automate killing cassettes with this pattern. It takes an iota and dequeues the cassette with that label if it exists.

killall.d: Terminates all cassettes, similar to the effects of the Parallel Processing mishap.

imbue_equipment.d: Imbues the supplied hexes into the Amethyst equipment in my other hand, so that they will be cast whenever the item is used. Costs 9 Charged Amethyst except on arrows, which cost 5 Shards.

similar.d: Pushes whether two patterns have same shape but not necessarily the same stroke order.

serialize_pattern.d: Turns a pattern into a list of numbers for my splitting, analysis, and dissection. The inverse of Calligrapher's Purification.

deserialize_pattern.d: Turns a list of numbers into a pattern for my viewing and execution. The inverse of Chirographer's Purification.

draw_pattern.d: Takes a pattern and produces a normalized list of vectors. The z-component of these vectors is zero. I feel this may be useful for artistic Hexes.

piercing_raycast.d: Works similar to Archer's Distillation but accepts an additional identifier. It will pierce all blocks until it hits the block specified by the identifier.

piercing_surface_raycast.d: Works similar to Architect's Distillation but accepts an additional identifier. It will pierce all blocks until it hits the block specified by the identifier.

entity_width.d: Similar to Stadiometer's Purification but pushes the width of an entity rather than its height.

main_index_for_each.d: Casts like Djehuty's Gambit, however each sub-execution operates on the main stack instead of copies of the stack.

get_mind_hex.d: Pushes the Hex stored in the provided mind, or Null if there isn't one.

set_mind_hex.d: Stores the provided Hex into the mind. If there is already a stored Hex, it will be overwritten. Costs one Charged Amethyst.

play_block_particle.d: Conjures a visual bit of debris, similar to that caused by breaking a block. Takes in a block identifier.

play_falling_dust_particle.d: Conjures particles similar to that caused by suspended gravity-affected blocks. Takes in a block identifier.

play_item_particle.d: Conjures a visual bit of fragments, similar to that caused by a tool breaking after wearing. Takes in an item iota.
